about:
# Upgrade Scout

**Finds the gear upgrades and consumables on the auction house that you can use and afford.** An addon for World of Warcraft Forever.

![Upgrade Scout: gear and consumables worth buying. One scan of the auction house shows what you can use and afford.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dibenkobit/upgrade-scout/main/docs/img/v2-6-0-cover.png)

**Download on [CurseForge](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/upgrade-scout) or [Wago](https://addons.wago.io/addons/upgrade-scout)**

English · [简体中文](https://github.com/dibenkobit/upgrade-scout/blob/main/docs/README.zh-CN.md) · [繁體中文](https://github.com/dibenkobit/upgrade-scout/blob/main/docs/README.zh-TW.md) · [Deutsch](https://github.com/dibenkobit/upgrade-scout/blob/main/docs/README.de.md) · [Русский](https://github.com/dibenkobit/upgrade-scout/blob/main/docs/README.ru.md) · [Français](https://github.com/dibenkobit/upgrade-scout/blob/main/docs/README.fr.md) · [Español](https://github.com/dibenkobit/upgrade-scout/blob/main/docs/README.es.md) · [Português](https://github.com/dibenkobit/upgrade-scout/blob/main/docs/README.pt-BR.md) · [한국어](https://github.com/dibenkobit/upgrade-scout/blob/main/docs/README.ko.md)

---

Open the auction house, click the **Upgrades** tab and press **Scan**. You get a list of gear that is
better than what you wear, slot by slot, with prices. Press **Buy** on the one you want.

The **Consumables** tab does the same for potions, elixirs, flasks, food, bandages and oils. It
lists the ones that add to your character and scores what each one adds. **Best for me** keeps one
of each kind: the one that gives you the most, at its lowest price. **Everything I can use** adds
what has no score: plain food and drink, healing and mana potions, bandages.

Away from the auction house, the tooltip of any item shows how much better it is than what you
wear: in your bags, in loot, in a quest reward and in a chat link.

![One scan shows what to buy: the Upgrades tab at the auction house](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dibenkobit/upgrade-scout/main/docs/img/v2-6-0-1-scan.png)

## What it does

- The scan shows only what you can equip right now and can pay for.
- The **Consumables** tab lists the potions, elixirs, flasks, food and oils that add to your
  character, the most useful first. **Everything I can use** in the **Filters** menu adds what
  has no score: plain food and drink, healing and mana potions, bandages.
- Marks two items in every slot: the **Best upgrade** is the strongest, the **Best value** is the
  cheapest per point of improvement.
- Every row has two prices: the **Buyout** and the **Net cost**, what the item costs you in the
  end. That is the buyout less what a vendor pays for it when you are done with it. Bought for 4
  silver and sold for 3, it cost you 1.
- **Best set for** picks the upgrades that give the most together for your gold, or for a sum you type.
- The **Filters** menu narrows the list. **Best armor type for the class** leaves out armor
  lighter than the heaviest your character wears. **Upgrade at least** leaves out upgrades
  smaller than the percent you type. **Buyout up to** leaves out items that cost more than the
  sum you type: the **Best upgrade** in each slot is then the best one for that price.
- Shops for your other characters too. A button at the mailbox puts the gear you bought into a
  letter to them.
- Any item's tooltip shows how much better it is than what you wear, for every spec of your class,
  such as Arms, Fury and Protection for a warrior. In the addon's window you can keep one line,
  for the tree you play, and choose where the lines show: on the addon's tabs at the auction
  house, in the rest of the game, or nowhere.
- A green arrow on the icon of an item in your bags or bank means it is an upgrade you can put
  on now. A grey one: an upgrade once you reach its level.
- Works right after you install it. The **Profile** dropdown starts on the talent tree you have
  the most points in.
- A window on your first login shows what the addon does. There you can switch off the tooltip
  lines and the bag arrows. The addon's button at the minimap opens it again.
- Scores gear with its own stat weights for every talent tree, worked out with the
  [wowsims/forever](https://github.com/wowsims/forever) simulator. No other addon is needed.
- Use Pawn? Choose **Pawn** in the addon's window, and gear is scored on your Pawn scales, not on
  the addon's weights. The lists and the bag arrows go by them, and the tooltip lines are Pawn's own.
- Use Forever Companion? Choose **Forever Companion** there, and gear is scored on its scales. The
  lists go by them, and the tooltip line and the bag arrows are Forever Companion's own.
- Use Forever Leveling BiS? Choose **Forever Leveling BiS** there, and gear is scored the way it
  scores it, for the main spec you chose in it. The tooltip lines and the bag arrows are its own.

Any class, any level. English, Chinese (Simplified and Traditional), German, Russian, French,
Spanish, Brazilian Portuguese and Korean.

## Install

**Install from [CurseForge](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/upgrade-scout) or [Wago](https://addons.wago.io/addons/upgrade-scout)**

The CurseForge or Wago app does it all for you.

You need World of Warcraft Forever (1.60.1). No other addon is needed.

To install by hand:

1. Download `UpgradeScout-<version>-forever.zip` from [CurseForge](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/upgrade-scout), [Wago](https://addons.wago.io/addons/upgrade-scout)
   or from [GitHub releases](https://github.com/dibenkobit/upgrade-scout/releases).
2. Unpack it into `World of Warcraft\_forever_\Interface\AddOns`.
3. Restart the game.

## Good to know

- An item's score is the sum of its stats, each times its weight in your **Profile**. The profile
  starts on the talent tree you have the most points in. You can pick another in the dropdown.
- The weights are worked out for a level 60 character, so they are an approximation. Below 60,
  hit, crit, haste and expertise count for less, as simulations of leveling characters show.
- Stamina (except for tanks), and a healer's Intellect, Spirit and mana regeneration, are set by hand: a simulation of damage cannot tell what staying alive or running out of mana costs.
- Armor, shield block, defense, dodge and parry count on every profile: against Stamina, as much as they help the simulator's tank.
- A `~` after a profile's name means no simulation covers that tree yet and its weights are
  estimated.
- Prices are buyouts. Auctions that only take bids are skipped.
- The list appears before the prices are checked. Until an item is checked, its price is the
  lowest among its auctions and may turn out to be a bid. You can buy right away: the price is
  checked before any purchase.
- With **Value by net cost** ticked, **Best value** goes by the net cost, not the buyout. What you
  can afford, and **Best set for**, still go by the buyout: that is what you pay.
- **Top 5 per slot** keeps the list short. Turn it off to see every upgrade. Checking all their
  prices then takes longer, up to a few minutes on a busy auction house.
- **Upgrade** is how much better an item is than the one it replaces, in percent. **New** means
  the slot is empty. Points, such as `+6 pts`, mean what you wear there adds nothing on your profile.
- **Best armor type for the class** keeps the heaviest armor your character has learned to
  wear: leather for a hunter, mail once it has learned mail. Cloaks, rings, weapons and shields
  stay in the list. A mage, a priest and a warlock wear cloth alone and have no such box.
- **Upgrade at least** goes by the percent in the **Upgrade** column. An item for an empty slot
  always stays.
- **Buyout up to** is the most to pay for one item. **Best set for** has its own budget and
  does not use it.
- Each character has its own **Best armor type for the class** box, its own **Upgrade at
  least** number and its own **Buyout up to** sum. When you shop for another character, you
  see and set that character's.
- A yellow `*` after a name means the item has effects the score does not count, such as procs.
- Health and mana potions have no score: no weight puts a number on "restores 700 health".
- Boots "of the Tiger" and boots "of the Whale" are different items with different prices. The
  game's Sell tab shows all of them in one list, so the lowest price there can be for another item.

## Buying for another character

1. Log in to the other character once with the addon installed. The addon saves its gear, level
   and skills.
2. On the character at the auction house, pick the other character's profile in the **Profile**
   dropdown and press **Scan**.

The list is now for that character. The one you are playing still pays.

At a mailbox, take the gear you bought out of the mail. A button under the mail window then puts it
into a letter to that character. Check the letter and press **Send**. Consumables you send yourself.

The addon knows the other character as it was when you last played it. Log in to it again after it
levels up or changes gear.

## Commands

- `/upscout` opens the addon's window: what it does and its settings. At the auction house it
  opens the Upgrades tab.
- `/upscout stats` shows how long the last scan took.
- `/upscout stats` and an item (shift-click it into the chat line) shows each stat of the item,
  its weight in your profile and what they add up to.
- `/upscout forget Name` removes a deleted character from the dropdown.

## License

All rights reserved, see [LICENSE](https://github.com/dibenkobit/upgrade-scout/blob/main/LICENSE). The stat weights were worked out with
[wowsims/forever](https://github.com/wowsims/forever), and their share below level 60 with
[MythicSim's forever engine](https://github.com/sage3648/mythicsim-forever-engine). Both are under
the MIT license.

For developers: how to run the tests and make a release is in [DEVELOPMENT.md](https://github.com/dibenkobit/upgrade-scout/blob/main/docs/DEVELOPMENT.md).

releases.notes:
- **Forever Leveling BiS** can score your gear. In the addon's window, under **Who scores your
  gear?**, choose **Forever Leveling BiS**: the lists at the auction house then go by its scores,
  not by the addon's weights.
- Your character is scored for the main spec you chose in Forever Leveling BiS, with the numbers
  its own tooltip shows. To score for another spec, choose another main spec there: the lists
  follow. **Change in Forever Leveling BiS**, beside the spec, opens its settings.
- Until you choose a main spec there, Forever Leveling BiS scores for the first spec of your
  class, whatever your talents. The window says so, and the button reads **Choose in Forever
  Leveling BiS**.
- With Forever Leveling BiS chosen, its own tooltip lines say what an item is worth and its own
  arrows mark the upgrades in your bags, so the addon leaves its own out. Switch either off in
  its settings, and the addon's come back, by its scores. In the bank, where it draws no arrows,
  the addon's stay.
- A weapon is scored for the hand it would go in: the main hand and the off hand count
  differently, as they do in Forever Leveling BiS. A weapon it says your spec cannot use is not
  listed, and one it keeps out of a hand is not offered for that hand: a Subtlety rogue's main
  hand takes a dagger. No row says a weapon gains more than its own tooltip does.
- A list made for another of your characters goes by Forever Leveling BiS's weights for that
  character's class, spec and level. The **Profile** dropdown lists the specs. The addon's lines
  say whose score it is: **Upgrade Scout (Forever Leveling BiS score)**.
- The choice is for the whole account. Without Forever Leveling BiS, or with it switched off, the
  addon scores by its own weights.
- A price check the auction house leaves without an answer is asked again after about a second,
  not 8: the scan no longer seems stuck on it.
- The scoring no longer stands still for several seconds near its end. The list appears while
  the game is still loading the last few items, and those join it as they come.
- A few dozen rows of any scan are items the game never loads. The scan no longer waits for them
  or looks each of them up, so the scoring ends without a pause and the price checks are shorter.
- Right after a game update the game takes a while to load its items. The scan waits for them,
  and when the wait is long the status line says so and counts them down. If the game stops
  loading, the list says how many rows it is short of, and the next scan has them.
- The **Profile** dropdown names your other characters in full, first name and surname, without
  the realm.
- Prices that are not checked yet are no longer dimmed. A dimmed row looked like one you could
  not buy, and most of those prices are right.
- While the prices are checked, the status line says that some of them may be bids. The row's
  tooltip still says when its price is not checked yet.
- If you have Forever Leveling BiS, the window comes up once after the update to show you the
  choice.

- The list no longer waits for the prices. It appears as soon as the scan knows the items,
  each at the lowest price among its auctions, and the prices are checked after that.
- A price that is not checked yet is dimmed, and the row's tooltip says so. Once checked it
  turns bright or changes, or the row goes: the lowest price of an item can be a bid.
- You can buy while the prices are being checked. The item is looked up first, as before any
  purchase, and the box asks at its real price.

- With **Everything I can use** ticked, what adds to your character stands at the top of each
  heading, the highest score first. Food, drink and potions that only restore come after it.
  Before, they came first.
- The headings with something scored under them come first, and the ones with nothing scored
  after them. With everything listed, the list no longer opens with healing potions.

- The **Consumables** tab now lists only what adds to your character: the consumables that have
  a score on your profile. Before, it listed everything you could use, and the elixirs stood
  under rows of food, water and potions.
- **Everything I can use**, a new box in the **Filters** menu, brings the rest back: plain food
  and drink, healing and mana potions, bandages.
- When nothing for sale has a score, the list says so and names the box.

- **Forever Companion** can score your gear. In the addon's window, under **Who scores your
  gear?**, choose **Forever Companion**: the lists at the auction house then go by its gear
  scales, not by the addon's own weights. The **Profile** dropdown lists the scales, for your
  other characters too.
- The scale in use is the one Forever Companion has in use. Choose another in the **Profile**
  dropdown or in the addon's window, and it is chosen in Forever Companion as well.
- With Forever Companion chosen, its own line says what an item is worth and its own arrows
  mark the upgrades in your bags, so the addon leaves its own out. Switch either off in Forever
  Companion's options, and the addon's come back, on its scales.
- A list made for another of your characters is about that character. Forever Companion knows
  only the one you are playing, so in such a list the tooltip has the addon's lines, and
  neither Forever Companion's line nor its BiS lists. The addon's lines say whose score it is:
  **Upgrade Scout (Forever Companion score)**.
- The choice is for the whole account. Without Forever Companion, or with it switched off, the
  addon scores by its own weights as before.
- If you have Forever Companion, the window comes up once after the update to show you the
  choice.
- In a list for another of your characters, the game's own comparison no longer lies under
  the tooltip of what that character wears. It did with Shift held, or with the game set to
  always compare items.
